description:
A variadic extern's contract describes only its fixed parameters, so no call
that uses the variadic tail is inside it.

`extern "C" defp libc::open(path :: c_string, flags :: c_int, ...) :: c_int`
resolves to a two-parameter arrow; `libc::open(path, 0, 0o644 :: integer)`
builds a three-column activation row; `Types::match_arrow`
(src/compiler2/types/arrow_match.rs ~220) returns Invalid on the arity
mismatch. Today this is invisible because an extern's return is its raw
declared return. Once an extern's return is its contract applied to its row,
every tail-using call has no answer.

Fixtures: fixtures2/00015_variadic_open_jit.fz,
fixtures2/behavior/c_int_negative_return.fz,
`aot_variadic_open_creates_file_with_mode_bits`,
`compiler2_native_program_jit_runs_variadic_extern_through_compiler2_codegen`.

Paper: the declaration is the definition, so its contract must accept exactly
the calls the declaration accepts: the fixed parameters, then any number of
tail arguments each of the variadic domain `.agent/docs/externs.md` states
(integer or pointer; floats refused). Settle with a reader, before a builder,
how an arrow expresses a tail in the Types data model and which existing
authorities (match_arrow, coverage, the wire derivation) read it — one
representation, not a row truncation at one call site.
title: A variadic extern's contract does not describe its tail
